quote.text: Is it really so pleasant to die in harness? That is the feeling of many people: their desire for their work outlasts their ability to do it. They fight against their own bodily weakness, and they regard old age as a hardship on no other grounds than that it puts them on the shelf. The law does not make a man a soldier after fifty or a senator after sixty: men find it more difficult to gain leisure from themselves than from the
quote.author: Seneca
quote.aiInsight:
• Parenthood: Embrace the truth that each season of life brings its own strengths, and do not overburden your spirit by clinging to past roles or forcing abilities beyond their natural span.
  • Parenthood: Recognize that nurturing children means also learning when to rest and allow growth at its own pace—teaching that every phase has its rightful time and value.
  • Leadership: Understand that true leadership is not measured by relentless toil, but by the wisdom to know one’s limits and the humility to adapt as circumstances change.
  • Leadership: Let this insight guide you to inspire your team by balancing ambition with self-care, so that both you and your followers can flourish without being worn down by excess expectations.
  • Product Management: Just as aging brings natural constraints, a product’s lifecycle must be respected; be ready to pivot and innovate rather than clinging to outdated formats out of habit.
  • Product Management: Cultivate the perspective that the drive for continuous work should not come at the expense of creative renewal—allocate time for reflection and strategic pauses to ensure sustained excellence.
